title: `upper`, `lower`: Java's full Unicode mappings, in the JVM's default locale
verdict: `char_set: UTF8` with full mappings (`ß` → `SS`, final sigma); ASCII fast path
description: `upper` and `lower` map ASCII text byte by byte and anything else with Java's `String.toUpperCase()` and `toLowerCase()`: Unicode's full mappings, context included. `upper('ß')` is `SS`, `upper('ﬁ')` `FI`, `upper('straße')` `STRASSE` (the length grows from 6 to 7), `lower('İ')` `i̇` (two code points), `lower('ΣΑΣ')` `σας` with a final sigma, `upper('ǅ')` `Ǆ`, `lower('Ⅻ')` `ⅻ`.

The no-argument `toUpperCase()` uses the JVM's default locale, so a JVM started in a Turkish or Azeri locale maps `i` to `İ` (a setting outside Spark's own configuration). The probes ran in an English locale.
reference: `upper`, `lower` with `char_set: UTF8`, a black box (Rust's `str::to_uppercase`, Unicode's full mappings); Lean evaluates them on ASCII only. ST-10 records that Substrait leaves simple and full mappings open. Spark's mappings are Unicode's full ones, as Rust's are, under a locale without special casing.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `lower` of the UTF8_BINARY column turns `İo` into `i̇o`: `i` plus U+0307, two code points for one
`upper` of the same rows: `İo` → `İO`, ASCII rows upper-cased byte by byte

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
